en.cardTitle: react-aria-live: aria-live regions compatible with real screen readers
en.cardDesc: React library for dynamic announcements in aria-live regions (polite/assertive) compatible with VoiceOver on iOS/macOS, NVDA and JAWS, with useAnnouncer() hook and strict TypeScript typing.

articles.article9-p1: aria-live regions are the standard mechanism for announcing dynamic content to screen readers, but their real behavior differs between VoiceOver, NVDA and JAWS: the same pattern that announces in one reader stays silent in another. react-aria-live encapsulates those interoperability details in a minimal, typed API.
articles.article9-p2: The most common mistakes are mounting the live region together with the message (the reader is not observing it yet), changing aria-live dynamically, or assuming a text change is always announced. VoiceOver on iOS, for example, is especially strict about container node stability and mutation timing.
articles.article9-p3: The useAnnouncer() hook keeps the regions mounted from the first render and exposes two methods: announcePolite for routine notifications and announceAssertive reserved for critical errors. Internally it applies the techniques that maximize real compatibility: persistent nodes, atomicity and control of repeated messages.
articles.article9-p4: The library's compatibility matrix was validated with VoiceOver on iOS and macOS, NVDA and JAWS on Windows, documenting which combinations of aria-live, aria-atomic and status/alert roles announce reliably on each. It is the same empirical rigor applied by the ecosystem's linear auditors.
articles.article9-p5: The entire package is typed in strict TypeScript, turning usage errors (for example, trying to announce before mounting the region provider) into compile-time errors rather than production silences.
articles.article9-p6: The library is open source at github.com/ingelectronicadj/react-aria-live.
